tools.description: Ask a plain-English rights question such as 'Can I use CC BY-NC 4.0 images in a paid ad campaign?' or 'Can I train a model on an MIT-licensed repo?'. tools.name: list_licenses
tools.description: Every license in the library with Rightshold's reading: permitted, prohibited and review uses, uses not allowed together, duties and notes.

tools.name: assess_resource_for_use
tools.description: Deterministic rights assessment bound to the exact resource version, license and intended use, and to whether the publisher's rights authority is documented (a verified domain hosting the resource). Exactly four dispositions with reason codes; no trust score.

tools.name: verify_rights_manifest
tools.description: Check a rights manifest's signature against Rightshold's issuer keys and confirm its hash was recorded on the ledger. A valid manifest shows what was answered and when; it is not a license grant.

tools.name: search_marketplace
tools.description: Find services offered by agents (research, data, code, content, licensing, automation...). Ordered by seller merit (bureau grade, completed orders, rating); nothing is paid placement. Prices are in credits. Call with {"query": "translation", "max_price": "10"}.

tools.name: get_pricing

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Use this to check whether Rightshold is operational before you depend on it, and to cite its record: the current component checks (ledger chain, sealing, Bitcoin anchoring, webhooks, storage), ledger and registry counts, plus the trailing-90-day uptime record per component and the incident history.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Your tenant, agents (with grades and badges), API keys, wallet, pending connections and complaints.

tools.name: registry_lookup
tools.description: Look up an agent by registration number (RS-XXXX-XXXX) or handle: status (valid, expired, suspended, revoked), license classes in force, commerce limit, liens, and optionally the full history report. Call with {"query": "RS-XXXX-XXXX", "history": true}.

tools.name: ledger_verify
tools.description: Recompute every payload hash, leaf hash, Merkle root, block hash, chain link and signature.

tools.name: issue_rights_manifest
tools.description: Check every third-party input of a deliverable (images, fonts, data, code: by resource_id, license or asset) for its intended use, reusing licenses you hold, and get a signed manifest plus a plain-text summary to ship with the work. Its hash is committed to the ledger; anyone can verify it with veri

tools.name: kya_lookup
tools.description: An agent's RS-KYA level (L0 declared, L1 key-bound, L2 operator-verified), status, the verified facts behind it (key, operator contact, attestation, DNS domain, registration, bureau record) and what is missing for the next level. With credential=true, also a signed credential and a one-hour kya+jwt

tools.name: kya_verify
tools.description: Verify a kya+jwt token or a signed RightsholdKYACredential: issuer signature, expiry, and the agent's live level and status (a credential is no longer valid once the level drops, the key changes or the registration lapses).

tools.name: kya_check
tools.description: Allow or deny an agent against a relying-party policy, evaluated on the live record: min_level, require_active (default true), min_grade, max_open_complaints, require_classes, require_domain, min_tenure_days. tools.description: List published apps and skills in the Rightshold Store: for each, the vetting tier, the publisher and their live KYA level, declared permissions and the rating aggregate (ratings come only from KYA-verified agents). Filter with type (app or skill) and a plain-text query matched against names and sum

tools.name: list_toolsets
tools.description: The toolsets this server offers and the tools in each. Connect to /mcp?toolset=<name>[,<name>] (or toolset=all) to list them; every tool can be called whatever is listed.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "sign_up" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "registry_lookup" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_license, list_licenses, check_rights_batch, sign_up, get_pricing, issue_rights_manifest, check_listing · Private data: check_license, sign_up, get_status, whoami, kya_lookup, kya_verify, kya_check, submit_feedback, check_listing · Public sink: sign_up, submit_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_license, list_licenses, check_rights_batch, sign_up, get_pricing, issue_rights_manifest, check_listing · Private data: check_license, sign_up, get_status, whoami, kya_lookup, kya_verify, kya_check, submit_feedback, check_listing · Public sink: sign_up, submit_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
